I don't understand the reasoning here. Is leaving it out overnight an attempt to keep it from getting .... stale? That sounds really counter intuitive to me. The only situation I can relate to this is that I know if you change the temperature of beer too quickly it can get skunky but I don't get how that applies to food.

I was in culinary class and we were taught that more than 90 minutes at room temperature is dangerous due to it allowing bacteria to grow. So maybe not from a 'freshness' standpoint, but at least from a hygienic standpoint, that stuff needs to get in the fridge asap. I rule in your favor. Maybe ask your friend for his reasoning so we can get a better understanding of his point of view?

There is scientific evidence (source: deep in my memory bank from who knows where) that if cooked food will be put in an airtight container and then in the fridge, it should be left out until it cools off. Something about moisture and the drastic temperature change being a good environment for bacteria/mold/whatever to flourish. So perhaps that is where roommate is coming from.

But overnight, no.

So, in my opinion, you are both wrong ;)

Well yeah I don't put hot food in the fridge. I cook some pasta, mix in the sauce, take it off heat, serve myself, eat (20ish minutes to cool down), then fridge it. I wouldn't put right off the grill food into the fridge.

it is NOT safe to put hot food straight in the fridge!! The warmth keeps bacteria away but as the food cools, the inside remains hot. In the end you have chilled food on the outside yet the inside is warm and rich for all the scum/bacteria of the world to start fuckin and making homes and just settling in.
yeah, as I had said I do not put hot food in the fridge. But it only takes 20 min or less to cool.

Your friend is making a dangerous mistake based on an urban legend or old wives tale that claims quick chilling is dangerous. Mistake number five here. Get it in the fridge within 1 to 2 hours based on room temperature.
